libraryStrings.pyodideMissingApi: Pyodide script loaded but loadPyodide() was not found.
libraryStrings.executionLimitExceeded: Program exceeded the execution time limit.
libraryStrings.tkinterBlockingUnsupported: This browser does not support blocking Tkinter dialogs. Use a browser with WebAssembly JSPI support.
libraryStrings.pythonHintSyntax: Check punctuation and brackets. A common issue is a missing colon after if/for/while/def/class.
libraryStrings.pythonHintIndentation: Check indentation. All lines inside a block need the same indentation level.
libraryStrings.pythonHintNameError: This name is unknown. Check spelling and make sure the variable was defined before use.
libraryStrings.pythonHintTypeError: The operation does not match the data type. Check what values your variables currently hold.
libraryStrings.pythonHintZeroDivision: You divided by zero. Check whether a variable can be 0 and handle that case before dividing.
libraryStrings.pythonHintIndexError: The index is outside the list. Check the length with len() - valid indices go from 0 to len(list) - 1. A loop over range(len(list)) stays one step too far if you use <=.
libraryStrings.pythonHintIntConversion: input() always returns a string. Convert it first, e.g. number = int(input()).
libraryStrings.pythonHintStringConcat: You are combining text with a number. Convert the number with str() or build the output with an f-string.
libraryStrings.pythonHintKeyError: This key does not exist in the dictionary. Check the exact spelling and whether the key was added before.
libraryStrings.pythonHintAttributeError: The object does not have this attribute or method. Check the type of the variable and the correct method name.
libraryStrings.pythonHintRecursion: The recursion never reaches its base case. Make sure the function has a condition that returns without calling itself again.
libraryStrings.pythonHintImport: The module or name cannot be imported. Check the spelling and whether the module is available in this environment.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainNameError: The name "{name}" is used but does not exist (yet). Either it is misspelled or it was never assigned a value before this point.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnboundLocal: The variable "{name}" is read inside a function before it has a value there. Assign it first or pass it in as a parameter.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainExpectedIndent: A line that ends with a colon needs an indented block below it, but the next line is not indented.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnexpectedIndent: This line is indented although no block was started above it. Remove the extra spaces.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnindent: This line is indented differently than the lines of its block. Lines in the same block need exactly the same indentation.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainMissingColon: A colon ":" is missing at the end of the line (after if, elif, else, for, while, def or class).
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnclosedBracket: The opening bracket "{bracket}" is never closed. Check that every opening bracket has a matching closing one.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnmatchedBracket: The closing bracket "{bracket}" has no matching opening bracket. Remove it or add the opening one.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainUnterminatedString: A text in quotes is not closed. Add the missing quotation mark at the end of the text.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainAssignVsCompare: A single "=" assigns a value. To compare two values, use "==".
libraryStrings.pythonExplainPrintParens: In Python 3, print needs parentheses: print("...").
libraryStrings.pythonExplainMissingComma: Two values are next to each other without a separator. A comma is probably missing.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainSyntaxGeneric: Python cannot read this line. Look closely at this line and the one above it for a missing bracket, quote or colon.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainTextNumber: Text (str) and numbers cannot be joined with "+". Convert the number with str(...), or use an f-string; convert input with int(...) if you want to calculate.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainOperandTypes: The operator "{operator}" cannot be used with the types "{left}" and "{right}".
libraryStrings.pythonExplainNotSubscriptable: A value of type "{type}" cannot be indexed with [ ]. Only lists, strings, tuples and dictionaries can.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainNotCallable: A value of type "{type}" is called like a function with ( ). Check for a variable that has the same name as a function.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainTooManyArguments: The function "{function}" expects {expected} argument(s), but was called with {given}.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainMissingArguments: The call of "{function}" is missing the argument(s): {arguments}.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainNotIterable: A value of type "{type}" cannot be looped over. A for loop needs e.g. a list, a string or range(...).
libraryStrings.pythonExplainNoneValue: A value is None ("nothing"), but the program treats it like a real value. A function without return gives back None - check whether a return is missing.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainAttributeError: A value of type "{type}" has no attribute or method "{attribute}". Check the spelling and the type of the variable.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainModuleAttribute: The module "{module}" has no function or value "{attribute}". Check the spelling.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainZeroDivision: A number is divided by 0, which is not possible. Check which variable is 0 at this point.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainIndexError: The position you access does not exist in the list or text. The last valid index is len(...) - 1; the first is 0.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainKeyError: The key {key} does not exist in the dictionary. Check the spelling or test with "in" first.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainInvalidNumber: The text {value} cannot be converted into a number. Make sure only digits are entered (and possibly a decimal point).
libraryStrings.pythonExplainRecursion: The function calls itself too often without ever stopping. A base case that ends the recursion is missing or never reached.
libraryStrings.pythonExplainModuleNotFound: There is no module "{name}" in this environment. Check the spelling of the import.
libraryStrings.pythonTutorPrivacyHint: Visualizing the code step-by-step opens pythontutor.com in an embedded frame. Your current code is sent to pythontutor.com to render the visualization.
libraryStrings.pythonDiagnosticsLoading: The IDE is still loading the type checking tools. Style and type hints will appear in the editor in a moment.
